verses.62:4: Porque a vossa misericórdia é melhor {vitas}: * os meus lábios vos louvarão.
verses.62:5: Assim vos bendirei {invita}: * e no vosso nome levantarei as minhas mãos.
verses.62:6: Que a minha alma {repleatur} como {adipe}: * e com lábios de exultação {laudabit}.

decisions.why: *vigiláre* is to keep awake, to keep watch (the Greek ὀρθρίζω πρὸς σέ, 'I rise early towards you', is the dawn verb; the Latin makes it a vigil). *vigio* keeps the Latin's word; *para vós* keeps *ad te* as a direction, not an object (*vigiar por* / *velar por* would be heard as 'watch over you'). The colon is also the Lauds antiphon *Deus, Deus meus, * ad te de luce vígilo* (grep: Psalmi major, Quadp1-0, Quadp2-0) and must read alone — it does. *estou desperto* is the plain sense of the vigil but a copula + adjective for a verb; *madrugo* is the Greek's verb, not the Latin's.

options.label: para vós vigio
options.note: Ruling; the Latin's verb, *ad te* as direction.

options.label: para vós estou desperto
options.note: the vigil said plainly; copula + adjective.

options.label: por vós madrugo
options.note: ὀρθρίζω, the Greek's dawn verb; not the Latin's word.

options.label: em vós estou vigilante
options.note: MS1932 (*em ti estou vigilante*); *em* for *ad* blurs the direction.

decisions.why: *de luce* is the Latin idiom for 'at daybreak, from first light' (DRB 'at break of day', MS1932 *desde o raiar da aurora*). *desde a aurora* is plain and ends the verse on a paroxytone; *desde a luz* keeps the Latin noun but is heard as 'since the light (existed)'. *ao romper da luz* keeps *lux* and the idiom but is two syllables longer.

options.label: desde a luz
options.note: the literal tier; misheard as 'since light began'.

decisions.why: The Latin leaves *sitívit* to be understood in the second colon (ποσαπλῶς σοι ἡ σάρξ μου). Kept verbless, as MS1932 and DRB keep it; *tibi* kept as *por vós* (DRB 'for thee'), so the flesh's thirst is towards God as the soul's is. Supplying *vos deseja* (DM1962, from the Hebrew *kamah*) would add a verb the Latin lacks. The exclamation is the Latin's *quam*. **v2:** the stylist heard *por vós* boxed in by commas and the colon stall; his *e de quantos modos a minha carne, por vós!* is taken — the same words, a supplied *e* (grammar, D2), *por vós* moved to the close where it lands on the oxytone. Still verbless, as the Latin. **v2 gate:** the Latinist (minor) calls the supplied *e* harmless but not in the text. Held: it is the conjunction the stylist needed to make the verbless colon sayable (grammar, D2); the asyndetic line is option 3 (*de quantos modos a minha carne, por vós!* is reachable by dropping *e* — added as an option).

options.label: e de quantos modos a minha carne, por vós!

forms.multipliciter: e de quantos modos a minha carne, por vós!

options.note: Ruling (v2); the stylist's line; verbless, *tibi* kept at the close.

options.label: de quantos modos, por vós, a minha carne!

forms.multipliciter: de quantos modos, por vós, a minha carne!

options.note: Draft 1; *por vós* between commas stalled the colon (stylist).

options.label: e de quantas maneiras a minha carne!

forms.multipliciter: e de quantas maneiras a minha carne!

options.label: de quantos modos a minha carne vos deseja!

forms.multipliciter: de quantos modos a minha carne vos deseja!

options.note: supplies a verb (the Hebrew's); refused under D2.

options.label: de quantos modos a minha carne, por vós!

forms.multipliciter: de quantos modos a minha carne, por vós!

options.note: the Latinist's v2 gate; asyndetic as the Latin.

decisions.why: *ínvius* is 'without a road, impassable' (L&S; ἄβατος). Three privative adjectives in a row, joined by *et … et*; *sem caminho, e sem água* keeps the privative echo (*in-via / in-aquosa* → *sem caminho / sem água*) and the *via → caminho* word. The first *et* is dropped for Portuguese listing (*deserta, sem caminho, e sem água*); the second kept. *intransitável* (MS1932) is exact but heavy and technical. **Accidental echo:** none at the cadence.

options.label: sem caminho
options.note: Ruling; keeps *via* and the privative pair.

options.label: e sem caminho
options.note: both *et* kept: *Em terra deserta, e sem caminho, e sem água*.

decisions.why: The *sancta / sanctum (a place)* row: *no lugar santo* (21:4 *in sancto hábitas*, 19:3 *de sancto*); ἐν τῷ ἁγίῳ. The row notes that *in sancto* 'is not always a place' — here it is (the psalmist comes before God in the sanctuary as he did, thirsting, in the desert: *sic*). *santuário* stays *sanctuárium*'s.

ὤφθην σοι, 'I was seen by you / I appeared before you' — the worshipper presenting himself at the sanctuary (the idiom of appearing before the Lord at the feasts). *vos apareci* is heard as an apparition; *me apresentei a vós* (MS1932) says the act, and ends the colon on an oxytone. *apareci diante de vós* keeps the verb and loses nothing but two syllables.

options.label: me apresentei a vós
options.note: Ruling; MS1932; DRB 'have I come before thee'.

options.label: vos apareci
options.note: the literal tier; heard as an apparition.

decisions.why: The Latin's plural (ὑπὲρ ζωάς; DRB 'than lives') is kept: *do que as vidas*. *super* after a comparative is 'than' (DRB), not 'above'. MS1932 adds *todas*. The singular *do que a vida* (DM1962, the Hebrew's sense) is smoother and closes the plural's openness (many lives, or life in all its forms).

'In my life, while I live' (ἐν τῇ ζωῇ μου). *na minha vida* is the Latin word for word and MS1932's (*em minha vida*); DRB 'all my life long' interprets duration. The same words close the Lauds antiphon *Lábia mea * laudábunt te in vita mea, Deus meus* (grep, Psalmi major) — both read alike.

options.label: enquanto eu viver
options.note: the sense as a clause; loses the noun that echoes 62:4 *vitas*.

decisions.why: Two words for fat (στέατος καὶ πιότητος): *adeps* is the soft fat, lard (L&S), *pinguédo* fatness (the family of *pinguis → gordo*). MS1932 has exactly this pair, *de banha e de gordura*, which keeps both and gives *pinguédo* the root its adjective has. The *adeps* row has *gordura* for 16:9b, where the word stands alone; here two words must be kept apart, and the row is open — noted there. DRB 'marrow and fatness' is its own gloss. *fartura* would make the second noun abundance, not fat — refused under D2 (the concrete image stays, rule 5). **v2:** the stylist (worst line) heard *banha* as a kitchen word that draws a smile and asked *de tutano e de gordura*. Refused: *tutano* (marrow) is DRB's gloss, not *adeps* (lard, the soft fat — L&S), and the Latin itself says fat twice (rule 2: the repetition and the image stay). His other complaint — the word at the head of the verse — is met by the reorder (decision `repleatur`): *banha* now stands mid-colon after *como de*. **For Gustavo's ear:** the price of the concrete image here is a homely word; *tutano* is kept as an option.

options.label: de banha e de gordura
options.note: Ruling; MS1932 word for word; L&S.

options.label: de gordura e de banha
options.note: keeps the *adeps* row's *gordura* (16:9b); the pingu-/gord- link lost.

options.label: de gordura e de fartura
options.note: the ear's line; the second noun becomes abundance.

options.label: de tutano e de gordura
options.note: the stylist; DRB's 'marrow'; not the Latin's word.

decisions.why: Jussive passive, 'may it be filled' (ἐμπλησθείη). *seja repleta* keeps the passive and the root; *se sacie* (MS1932 *seja saciada*) is *satiáre*'s verb (21:27 *serão saciados*). *adimplére → encher* is another Latin verb and Greek (πληρόω), so *se encha* is avoided. **v2:** the stylist found *seja repleta* stiff and the subjunctive hard to hear; *se farte* taken — a plain verb of being filled with food, the passive made reflexive (grammar, D2), and it is not *satiáre*'s *saciar*. The colon is reordered: the ambiguity reader heard *Como de banha* at the head of the verse as "I eat lard" (*como* = I eat). With *Que a minha alma se farte* first, *como* can only be "like". The order is grammar (D2).

options.label: se farte
options.note: Ruling (v2); the stylist's verb; the jussive with *Que*, the subject first.

options.label: seja repleta
options.note: Draft 1; the root and the passive; bookish (stylist).

decisions.why: The Latin has no object here (αἰνέσει τὸ στόμα μου), where 62:4 had *laudábunt te*. Kept objectless; the subject goes before the verb so that *a minha boca* is not heard as the object ('will praise my mouth'), and the verse closes on the oxytone. MS1932 and DRB supply 'thee' — option.

options.label: a minha boca louvará
options.note: Ruling; no object, as the Latin.

options.label: louvará a minha boca
options.note: the Latin's order; *a minha boca* can be heard as the object.

decisions.why: The *lectus / stratum* row: *stratum → cama* (6:7, 40:4), *leito* for *lectus*. *super* is 'on' the bed; *na minha cama* is how Portuguese says it (40:4 took *no leito* for *super lectum* from the stylist). *sobre a minha cama* is the letter. *no meu leito* (MS1932) crosses the row. **v2:** the stylist found *cama* flat beside *madrugadas* and asked *no meu leito*. Refused: *leito* is *lectus*'s word in the row, and the pair *leito / cama* is how 6:7 and 40:4 keep *lectus* and *stratum* apart; *cama* is plain and concrete (rule 5). His line is option 3.

The neuter plural 'in the mornings / the morning hours' (ἐν τοῖς ὄρθροις, the dawn watches; DRB 'in the morning'). Also the versicle *In matutínis, Dómine, meditábor in te. R. Quia fuísti adjútor meus* and a Lauds antiphon (grep) — the colon reads alone. *mane → de manhã* and *dilúculo → ao amanhecer* are taken (rows), so this keeps its own plural: *nas madrugadas* is the dawn hours the Greek names and the Latin plural. 72:14 *castigátio mea in matutínis* should follow.

Copies 60:5 *ao abrigo das vossas asas*, as the *tegmen* row asks (*velaméntum* and *tegmen* share the Greek σκέπη; D15). 60:5's Latinist asked twice for *sob o véu* / *sob a cobertura*, held there; both stay options here.

options.label: sob a cobertura
options.note: DRB 'under the covert'; refused by the *tegmen* row.

decisions.why: *adhærére → apegar-se* for the soul, as 118:25 *A minha alma apegou-se ao chão* and 118:31 *Apeguei-me aos vossos testemunhos* (same Greek ἐκολλήθη). *post te* (ὀπίσω σου) is 'behind you, after you' — the soul clinging as it follows. Portuguese cannot say *apegou-se atrás de vós* or *após vós* (D43's *após* is after a verb of motion); DRB ('stuck close to thee') and MS1932 (*está presa a ti*) both let the preposition go. Ruled *apegou-se a vós*, with the loss recorded; *seguiu-vos de perto* keeps the following and loses the clinging. The colon is also an antiphon (St Stephen, St Lawrence: *Adhǽsit ánima mea post te, quia caro mea…*) and reads alone. **v2:** the Latinist (minor) asked for *post te* back, with this very fix. Taken: the following behind is the Latin's image (D2 keeps images), and the participle supplies no sense the preposition lacks. The colon still reads alone as the antiphon. **v2 gate:** the Latinist (minor) now finds *apegou-se a vós, seguindo-vos* renders *post te* twice and asks *apegou-se atrás de vós*. Held: that is not a Portuguese sentence (one clings *to*, not *behind*), and the participle is the fix he proposed himself on v1; his new line is an option.

options.label: apegou-se a vós, seguindo-vos
options.note: Ruling (v2); the Latinist's fix; *post* kept by a participle.

options.label: apegou-se a vós
options.note: Draft 1; *post* lost (Latinist, minor), as DRB and MS1932.

options.label: seguiu-vos de perto
options.note: the idiom's sense; loses the clinging.

options.label: apegou-se atrás de vós
options.note: the Latinist's v2 gate; the preposition to the letter; not idiomatic.

decisions.why: 'the lower parts of the earth' (τὰ κατώτατα τῆς γῆς; DRB 'lower parts'). *as profundezas da terra* is the plain word for the lowest places (MS1932 *profundidades*); *as partes inferiores* is the letter and sounds anatomical. 138:15 *in inferióribus terræ* should follow. **v2:** the Latinist (minor) asked for the Latin's comparative, proposing *nas partes inferiores*. The comparative taken, his word refused: *partes inferiores* is heard as the lower body. *as partes mais baixas da terra* (DRB) keeps *inferióra* as a place and a degree, at no length cost against the Latin colon. 138:15 *in inferióribus terræ* should follow.

options.label: nas partes mais baixas
options.note: Ruling (v2); the Latin's comparative, DRB's 'lower parts'.

options.label: nas profundezas
options.note: Draft 1; plain, but the comparative lost (Latinist, minor).

decisions.why: The hands of the sword (εἰς χεῖρας ῥομφαίας) is the Latin's image and stays (rule 5); *entregues nas mãos de* is current Portuguese for handing over. MS1932 *ao poder da espada* explains the image.

*partes* 'shares, portions' (μερίδες; DRB 'the portions of foxes'): what falls to the foxes. *serão a porção das raposas* makes the plural a collective. MS1932 *presa das raposas* interprets (prey). The plural *as porções* is the letter.

*juráre in* + ablative is to swear by (ὀμνύων ἐν αὐτῷ; DRB 'swear by him', MS1932 *juram por ele*). *nele* would be the letter and is not Portuguese for an oath. *eo* is open between God and the king, as in the Latin; *por ele* keeps it open.

*obstrúere* is to block, stop up (L&S; ἐνεφράγη). *foi fechada* is plain (MS1932); *foi tapada* keeps the stopping-up image but in Brazil *tapar a boca* is to cover it with a hand. Once in the psalter (grep).

options.label: foi tapada
options.note: the letter; DRB 'stopped'; the stylist asked it (refused: a hand over the mouth).

decisions.why: The neuter plural *iníqua* → *coisas iníquas*, as 25:4 (*iníqua geréntibus → os que fazem coisas iníquas*); *iniquidades* is *iníquitas*'s word. DRB 'wicked things'. **v2:** the stylist found *coisas* a filler and asked *foi tapada a boca dos que falam o que é iníquo*. Refused: *coisas iníquas* is 25:4's wording for the same neuter plural (rule 6), and *tapada* is heard in Brazil as a hand over the mouth (decision `obstructum`). *o que é iníquo* is an option.

choices.62:2a: *Deus, Deus meus → Deus, meu Deus*, as 21:2 and 42:5 (the vocative without *ó*, as the finished psalms). The colon is the Lauds antiphon. checks: the second colon is +4 by the counter, which does not elide *desde‿a‿aurora*; the first colon is −3, so the verse is level with the Latin.
choices.62:2b: *sitíre in → ter sede de*, the perfect kept (*teve*), as the settled row (D42; 41:3). checks (v2): *vós … vós* at mediant and final is flagged as rhyme — the Latin has the same echo (*ánima mea … caro mea*) and the same object (*in te … tibi*); accepted.
choices.62:3: *virtus → poder* (row). The ‡ after the first colon kept. The first colon is verbless, as the Latin. checks: the second colon +4 (*me apresentei a vós*, decision `apparui`); *vos apareci* would save it at the cost of an apparition — accepted. The ambiguity reader did not hear the comparison *as in the desert, so in the holy place*: it is the Latin's *sic* with the comparison unstated; not supplied (D2: an ambiguity the Latin leaves).
choices.62:5: *benedícere* (man → God) *→ bendizer* with the accusative (*vos bendirei*). *leváre → levantar* (row; 118:48 *levantei as minhas mãos*). *in nómine tuo → no vosso nome* (53:3).
choices.62:6: *exsultátio → exultação* (row; 41:5b *com voz de exultação*). *exultação* listed as unknown again by the ambiguity reader (the row records it; kept).
choices.62:7: *Si memor fui* kept conditional (*Se me lembrei*), as the Latin and DRB; MS1932 flattens to a statement. *memor esse → lembrar-se de*, *meditári in → meditar em* (rows). *adjútor → auxílio* (row, 14/14); *fuísti → fostes*. The versicle *In matutínis, Dómine, meditábor in te. R. Quia fuísti adjútor meus* reads from the two colons. The ambiguity reader found the conditional *Se me lembrei* odd and heard "whenever" as a second reading; the Latin's *Si* is kept (DRB *If*). He listed *auxílio* as unknown (the row, 14/14; kept).
choices.62:8b: *suscípere* (persons) *→ amparar* (D19); *a vossa direita me amparou* = 17:36a word for word. The colon *Me suscépit déxtera tua* is a Lauds antiphon (grep). *exsultáre → exultar*. checks (v2): the flex colon +5 and closing on the enclitic *seguindo-vos* (stress on *-guin-*) — the cost of keeping *post te* (decision `post`); accepted.
choices.62:10: *quǽrere ánimam → buscar a minha alma* (row; 53:5), with the row's known cost (heard as the spiritual soul before 'my life'). *vero → porém*, repeated in 62:12 as the Latin repeats it. *trádere → entregar* (row). checks: the last colon +4; it carries two Latin members (*tradéntur in manus gládii · partes vúlpium erunt*), neither can go — accepted.
choices.62:12: *lætári in → alegrar-se em*; *laudári → ser louvado* (row; 33:3): the Latin's passive (ἐπαινεσθήσεται), not MS1932's *se gloriará*. checks: the last colon +4 (*coisas iníquas* for one neuter plural) — accepted. *iníquas* listed as unknown by the ambiguity reader; kept (the *iníquus* row). The ambiguity reader heard *por ele* first as God — the Latin leaves God and the king open.

audit.note: Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps062.md (Latin, LXX, Hebrew, DRB, MS1932, DM1962). Liturgical uses found by grep in content/do: Lauds antiphons *Deus, Deus meus, * ad te de luce vígilo*, *Lábia mea * laudábunt te in vita mea*, *In matutínis * meditábor in te*, *Me suscépit * déxtera tua*, *Benedícam te * in vita mea*; the versicle *In matutínis, Dómine, meditábor in te. R. Quia fuísti adjútor meus*; the antiphon *Adhǽsit ánima mea post te* (St Stephen, St Lawrence). Hard readings: 62:2a *de luce vígilo*, 62:2b the verbless second colon, 62:6 the two fats, 62:8b *post te*, 62:10 *partes vúlpium*.

Hard checks pass. Soft: 62:2a −3/+4 (level over the verse), 62:3‡ +4, 62:10* +4, 62:12* +4 — accepted, reasons in choices. No cadence rhyme flagged. 62:4b, 62:6b, 62:7†, 62:8b†* close on oxytones as the Latin's *te* allows.
